# api.openlyoperated.biz/v1

The read api over openly-operated business: the same JSON the pages on openlyoperated.biz render,
served to anyone. Business data — a firm's own books — is read through from the firm's own
account and never copied; the firm gates it. Economic data — what every firm emits as it trades —
is the platform's own store, no opt-in. The paths carry the line: /gerps/... is business data,
/economy/... is economic data.

Contract: openapi.json beside this file. /v1 is the stage; a breaking change is /v2 beside it.
Anonymous reads share the stage throttle. A key (x-api-key) in the keyed plan lifts it and is
metered per call.

## resources

- GET /gerps?q=&sector=&city=&state= — the directory: published, active gerps, each with its
  gerp_profile_id, published name, city, state, naics_intended, its sources ({key, kind, label},
  the gerp's own catalog) and api (/v1/gerps/<gerp_id>). Cached a minute.

- GET /gerps/{gerp_id}/sources — the gerp's own catalog: {gerp_id, sources: [{key, kind, label}]}.
  404 for a gerp that does not publish.
- GET /gerps/{gerp_id}/sources/{source} — the read-through: the gerp's own /oob/<source>, byte for
  byte, streamed as it arrives, the query string passed through (financials, inventory, metrics,
  and whatever a module publishes next). The gerp's own 404 and 429 are yours. Business data —
  a firm's own tables, read from its own account, never copied.

- GET /gerps/{gerp_id}/metrics?grain= — the firm's product record as the platform counted it:
  one metric per event and measure the firm recorded (`<event>.<kind>`: `account.signed_up.count`,
  `session.started.count_distinct`, `revenue.posted.sum`), in the metric shape {key, label, unit, grain, class, headline,
  points, definition, source}, points at the asked grain (day by default; week; month). `class`
  is the vocabulary's bucket for the event. Beside them, one card per catalogue ratio
  (`<bucket>.<name>`: `membership.churn`, `saas.margin`; unit ratio or USD) whose every leg the
  firm has recorded, composed from the leaves. Every published firm's every product event counts;
  nothing is asked of the gerp, and a set's size is served, never a member. 404 when the gerp
  does not publish.
- GET /gerps/{gerp_id}/metrics/{slug}?grain= — one of them.
- GET /economy/counters?signal=&from=&to= — economic data, the first store: the counters every
  gerp's events add to (revenue, expense; margin derived), by month, in the metric shape
  {key, label, unit, grain, headline: {period, value}, points: [{period, value}], definition,
  source: {curl}}. No signal names the catalog. Every gerp, published or not — the terms-of-use
  baseline — and never a gerp id.

## the stream

- GET /events?channel=/oob/counters — every counter delta as it lands, as server-sent events:
  data is {key, op, magnitude, period, at}. Economic data: every gerp, no gerp id, no event.
- GET /events?channel=/oob/<gerp_id>/<kind> — a published gerp's events of one kind as they
  happen (journal_entry-posted, distribution-paid, ...: the detail-type with dots and underscores
  as dashes). data is {kind, gerp_id, at, detail}, the detail projected through the event's
  contract — a field naming a person or a secret is never on it.
- Both need x-api-key; a held stream costs what a request throttle cannot see. Frames: `id:` a
  millisecond timestamp, `event:` the channel, `data:` the JSON, a comment heartbeat every 15s,
  `: reconnect` before the relay ends at ~14 minutes — reconnect and continue.
- The same channels over WebSocket, no relay: wss://events.openlyoperated.biz/event/realtime
  with the AppSync Events protocol and the public subscribe key (subscribe-only; the key is on
  the page). SSE is the contract; the socket is the convenience.

## how to extend it

A resource is a folder under api/v1/ and a path in openapi.json naming it (x-backend) and whether
it streams (x-stream) and whether it needs a key (x-keyed). handler.py or handler.mjs makes a
lambda; a Dockerfile makes a service. A test fails when a path and a folder disagree, or when this
file does not name a path.
